name: Lufthansa City (2018 livery)
description: Lufthansa's 2018 livery with the title 'Lufthansa City': 'Lufthansa' in dark blue and 'City' in a lighter blue, over the forward windows. Otherwise as Lufthansa: white fuselage, dark-blue fin and rear fuselage on a straight diagonal, the white crane in a ring on the fin.

sources.note: ICAO LHX, callsign CITYAIR; brand 'Lufthansa City'; A319, A320neo, A220-300 on order.

logos.description: The Lufthansa crane (Kranich): a stylised flying crane, wings raised in a V, neck stretched forward, inside a thin ring; white line art on the dark blue.
Small dark-blue crane in a ring under the cockpit windows.
Small dark-blue crane in a ring near the top of the sharklet's outer face.

titles.style: Lufthansa Head: a bold, slightly tight grotesque, mixed case, upright, over the forward windows.

notes: Geometry follows Lufthansa's 2018 livery (DLH/standard); only the title differs. Not drawn: type and city name small under the windows, registration and flags ahead of the blue block, 'Member of Lufthansa Group'. Re-checked 2026-11-15: the blue block's forward edge now follows Lufthansa's as re-measured on the A320 in the 2026-11-15 pilot (a curve meeting the crown at x 0.8, smooth); the same paint is applied to the same A320neo airframes, and D-AIJR (2026-06-09) shows it so, though too obliquely to re-measure. The title (x 0.16-0.40, crossing the windows' top) agrees with D-AIJR; lowercase ~0.70 of the capitals.
history: New in the dataset; Lufthansa City Airlines began scheduled flights on 26 June 2024 (Wikipedia). The 'Lufthansa City' title came with the later public brand name; its first paint date isn't confirmed here.
